What is your current status? Drugs have been a secondary character in my life, but I have rules to stop it from overcoming me. What is your withdrawal? What are you taking to alleviate any issues?

The thing no one tells you is that the physical withdrawals are terrible, but the PAWS (post-acute withdrawals symptoms) are worse as they wear you down. I'm not a master, but I do enjoy the neurochemistry of drugs. As much as withdrawals are terrible, they slowly fade by the minute - it is your willpower that is tested. Don't feel bad about sleeping constantly for a week, or having odd sexual urges for a sense of feeling within your reality. Drugs use requires you to "pay the piper" in the end and how you balance that "payment" is critical.

Suffering is the payment you ignored during the benefit and now your body aches. It will recover and you can aid it on the way, but if you slip up you reset the clock. Every minute gained is a minute earned. Accept you will suffer for 2-3 weeks and write it off. Your job is recovery now, as devastating as it may be you can build towards recovery.

I'm not taking any drugs (not yet anyway), I just started seeing certain specialists. I have a diet plan and all that, I'm fine physically but not emotionally, and that is what always prevents me from relapsing.

I completely missed the letters ED. This is outside my my expertise, but I hope for all the best. Addiction is based on a neurochemical pattern and I find understanding your biochemical mechanism helpful to your state.

The benefit you have is that EDs are not as unforgiving as drug addiction in that relapse will not be a biochemical reset. You have a psychological loop that activates. Your ED is activated by stimuli, those stimuli cause biochemical signaling and neuronal patterns which cascade into behavior. The great thing is that you can recover! We know this is true as brains adapt to new environments.

At a core level your ED is based on something - a desire to X. Why X? Why do you hold that value? What do you want from your life? It is an addiction, but it is a subconscious conclusion attempting to solve a problem. Unfortunately understanding the addiction cannot simply overcome the pattern of behavior.

The brain works by enforcing any neuronal pathway it activates, this is called Hebbian Learning. Your brain is solving an issue and you receive a benefit from it as it solves that issue. This mechanism is the core structure of your behaviour - this is how you are capable of everything. The danger is that negative actions are also carried along. Hebbian learning results in strengthening behaviors as it makes it easier for neurons to fire for the next occurrence. So what does this mean for you?

This means the most difficult change of experience is at the beginning. As you start to reduce that neuronal firing it is forced to be stronger to achieve the same result. This means that you can have stronger, but less frequent urges in the future - however now you know that is objectively true. Every step you take towards recovery may feel emotionally worse, but it is a lashing out of a dying pathway. When you hold your breath for an extended time your brain activates and tries to override your conscious decision to hold your breath. You feel a stronger and stronger sense of panic and desperation. The pathway is activated as it needs to accomplish a goal - you are trying to change the goal. The more you reduce the behavior the more panic your brain will produce, but never forget - this means you are winning. The pathway is desperate to survive and you are killing it - killing it because it is detrimental. The brain is pattern-based and you are changing the pattern.

Even if you relapse once in a while don't despair as those moments when you override the urge you are dampening the pathway. If you relapse 1/5 times you are still harming the pathway those other 4 times! Addiction is a long grind, a marathon not a sprint. Losing one day here or there is nothing compared to a period of change over months. Remember what you desire, remember what you are striving for, and remember that your body is performing an unconscious rhythm, not a desire. The desire is the action you wish to take not the action your body is forcing you to take. Your body and brain are one machine that can control one another. You can tear away its power a day at a time.

I wish you all the best and if you any questions I'll gladly answer them. You've isolated a change in your life - and you can achieve it!
